slides.eyebrow: A new way to shape your story
slides.title: Good ideas deserve a great stage.
slides.body:
From a rough thought to a presentation that moves.
Built with you. Refined with your agent.
slides.notes: Open with the idea, not the tool. This sample deck demonstrates the authoring system; replace it with your own story.

slides.title: The first draft is just the beginning.
slides.body: Your thinking evolves. Your presentation should keep up.
bullets: Start with a conversation, not a blank slide.
Change one idea without rebuilding the deck.
See every revision as soon as it is saved.
slides.notes: Ask the audience how often the story changes after the first draft. Explain that stable slide IDs make focused revisions possible.

slides.title: You direct. Your agent helps build.

cards.title: Find the story
cards.body: Clarify the audience, the takeaway, and the decision you want to inspire.

cards.title: Make it visible
cards.body: Turn the outline into expressive layouts, diagrams, and purposeful motion.

cards.title: Refine together
cards.body: Ask questions. Challenge the argument. Edit a slide. Watch it improve.

slides.notes: Each card is a separate part of the iterative loop. The agent works on files; the browser gives you immediate visual feedback.

slides.title: Motion should explain the idea.
slides.body: Reveal relationships. Guide attention. Give the important moment room to land.
slides.notes: Avoid animating everything just because it is possible. Prefer one visual argument and one motion language per slide. Reduced-motion preferences are respected.

slides.title: Your presentation stays yours.

metrics.label: Editable JSON source for the story, design, and notes
Starting layouts, plus custom HTML and JavaScript

slides.notes: These numbers describe this tool, not business performance. Export produces one HTML file. External media, if added, still require connectivity unless embedded.

slides.title: Better with every conversation.

steps.title: Brief
steps.body: Who is this for? What needs to change?

steps.title: Draft
steps.body: Build a clear narrative with a strong point of view.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: Preview the flow, timing, and visual hierarchy.

steps.title: Refine
steps.body: Make a focused edit. Rehearse. Repeat.

slides.notes: You can ask the agent questions without changing files. When a revision is requested, it should preserve unrelated slides and report what changed.

slides.title: What is your next big idea?
slides.body: Tell your agent the audience, the goal, and the time you have. Then make the first version together.
slides.notes: Close by inviting a concrete next step: start a new deck, ask for an outline, or revise this sample.
